reports.title: Keysight Technologies Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Results

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Keysight’s first fiscal quarter of 2027 revenue is expected to be in the range of $2.040 billion to $2.060 billion. Non-GAAP earnings per share for the first fiscal quarter of 2027 are expected to be in the range of $3.63 to $3.69. Certain items impacting the GAAP tax rate pertain to future events and are not currently estimable with a reasonable degree of accuracy; therefore, no reconciliation of GAAP earnings per share to non-GAAP has been provided. Further information is discussed in the section titled “Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below.

desk.headline: Revenue up 41% to $1.99bn and EPS $3.61, both beat; Q1 outlook of $2.04–2.06bn revenue and $3.63–3.69 EPS
results: Revenue jumped 41% to $1.99bn and orders rose 53% to $2.34bn, a record quarter.
Commercial communications, which includes AI data-centre testing, grew 73% to $1.15bn; aerospace and defence grew 7%.
The industrial segment grew 16% to $498m on semiconductor, automotive and energy demand.
Adjusted EPS nearly doubled to $3.61 from $1.91; GAAP EPS was $2.82.
Free cash flow was $465m for the quarter and $1.75bn for the year; the company ended with $2.92bn of cash.

guidance.summary: For Q1 fiscal 2027 Keysight expects revenue of $2.04–2.06bn and adjusted EPS of $3.63–3.69. On the call, management described a base case of about 20% revenue growth for fiscal 2027.

items.metric: Revenue growth (base case, from the call)

points: Management said AI-related bookings were about 2.5 times last year's level, with wireline testing growing at triple digits.
Wireless orders grew at double digits and the 6G business doubled; defence orders were strong on record budgets.
Supply is tight on a small group of AI-focused products, leaving extra hardware backlog; the company is adding capacity.
Gross margin is holding near 68% even after about one point of tariff cost.
Fiscal 2026 buybacks totalled $667m with $833m of authorisation left; Jason Carey takes over as CFO next month.

watch: Whether orders hold up after the expected seasonal dip from Q4 to Q1.
Supply constraints on AI-related test products and how fast the extra backlog ships.
